They either shut down the unauthorized launch sequence themselves in Russia, or they knew that the launch officers in the U.S. at Minot Air Force Base could shut down what they had put into... had initiated the launch sequence. (0:39:17)

So, I think they're just trying to make a point, you know, they're wagging a finger at us. But I've also said, and I've told my lecture audiences when I was speaking around the country over the decades, if they do have a long-term presence here, if they have bases, for example, under the ocean, if they have projects and plans that involve the earthly realm, a massive nuclear conflict would disrupt what they've got going on, in addition to whatever detrimental consequences that could be. (0:39:47)

Detrimental effects it would have, catastrophic effects it would have on human civilization. So, perhaps what they're doing is partially altruistic toward the human race, but probably self-serving as well in that regard. What about your own situation? Do you feel that they may have in any way prompted you to take such a passionate interest in this topic? As I said in this book I wrote with Bob Jacobs, because of this childhood, I didn't go into great detail about it, but this incident that I had as a child, and memories of it later in my childhood, I'm pretty sure that they have been a part of my life for most of my life. (0:40:31)

And who knows why I didn't have any sense of their presence after that childhood era, until I was 38 in 1988. Why the gap? Who knows? If they interacted with me in that interval, I have no memory of it. But, as I said in the book, because these incidents were ongoing, and because I really could not explain, I can't still to this day explain why I have been so driven, not only to research this, to investigate it, but I've had, not so much now because I'm not well and I don't do it anymore, but for decades I had the need to communicate this to the public. (0:41:12)

And I'm an introvert by nature. Speaking in front of lecture audiences was just something that was very difficult, but I felt it had to be done. There weren't too many people who had the information I had, and I felt it incumbent upon me to talk publicly about what I had learned from these military veterans. So, essentially, almost without exaggeration, my whole life for decades has revolved around this. And so, perhaps naturally, I have wondered over the years, is this my own idea? You know, was this my own game plan? Or was I really being subliminally, subconsciously prompted by these entities that I am quite clear I've had contact with? Were they in effect pushing me, nudging me down the road? (0:42:00)

I have no idea, but I don't think that's an unreasonable thought, or at least something to speculate about. So, you know, I don't think at this late in the game I'm going to have any answers to that. But yeah, I've given that serious thought. (0:42:15)

Seven of the 160 individuals that you've interviewed also reported this type of contact or abduction experience. It certainly suggests that it's not just an accidental or random event that's taking place, that it's part of a systematic effort to interact with humanity at some level. I think that's correct. And, you know, I can't quantify this in terms of the general population, but even among the 167 veterans that I've interviewed, seven may not seem like a significant number, but you've got seven people who had experiences, you know, they were either charged with operating or guarding nuclear weapons, and at other points in their lives, they had face-to-face alien abduction experiences. (0:43:09)

Some of your viewers may not know this. Bob Salas, who was involved in this missile shutdown at Malmstrom in March of 67, he kept his secret. I knew about it because we were friends. I knew about it for many years. But finally, in 2013, he went public and said that in 1985, he clearly had an abduction experience. And in my book, I have a chapter called Veteran Voices, where I describe some of the veterans who've talked to me about their apparent abduction experiences, go on the record and talk about what happened to them. (0:43:46)

So, again, most people know, you know, the great majority of people know about what Bob has talked about at Malmstrom Air Force Base, but virtually no one knows what happened at his home in California three decades later, two decades later. Let me cite one other individual who I consider utterly credible. (0:44:24)

A man named Mario Woods introduced himself to me in 2017. In 1977, he was a security policeman at Ellsworth Air Force Base, and he guarded what was called November Flight, a group of 10 missiles designated November. And long story short, there was alarms at one of the missiles one night in November. He can't remember what day in November. He remembers it was around Thanksgiving. He's at this launch control facility with the other security policemen, and suddenly there's alarms going off because this one missile was clearly having anomalies. Something had tripped the wires, so to speak, and there was an unauthorized presence at one of these missile sites. (0:44:53)

So Mario Woods and his partner raced out there, you know, gathered their weapons and rushed out there. And as they approached this missile site, I forget the designation, I want to say November 5. In any case, he saw, they both saw suddenly this huge spherical-shaped object. He said it was probably the size of a Walmart building hovering just a few feet above the ground above this missile silo. (0:45:21)

No sooner had that happened, suddenly it was as if all of the air was sucked out of the truck they were in. They suddenly were suffocating. They could not breathe. And no sooner had that happened, he saw out of his window small figures approaching the truck. And the next thing he knew, it was four hours later and that they were at an entirely different location. They had no memory of themselves and their trucks being transported, but apparently they were transported about five miles away. (0:45:54)

And in 2017, I arranged to have some regression hypnosis on Mario. And if one looks at the video, I've never seen anybody as terrified in my life. (0:46:07)

He clearly was in the moment reliving that encounter with these small entities. He was so scared, so terrified, he was trying to climb off the bed and hide while he was being regressed under hypnosis. And so he did remember encounters with non-human entities. And again, you know, someone whose job was to guard nuclear missiles, and yet he's having that kind of encounter as well. So on occasion, they do overlap. The missile cases or the nuclear cases and the abduction cases, there is a Venn diagram overlap sometimes. (0:46:47)

We seem to be in an era in which some form of disclosure is taking place. At one time, the government flatly denied that anything of any real scientific interest was occurring. Now we hear the possibility that maybe something is taking place, but they don't know what. I imagine that when events like this take place at a nuclear weapons facility, that the government has a process for debriefing the people involved and that the government is well aware of what has taken place. (0:47:25)

They're obviously aware, and virtually without exception, the people that I've interviewed who've had experiences out at the missile sites or other nuclear weapons related facilities have described being debriefed by what are called OSI agents, the Air Force Office of Special Investigations. And that goes on base after base, decade after decade. Those are the individuals that do the debriefing. In almost every case where they are debriefed, they're required to sign written non-disclosure statements stipulating severe penalties, legal penalties, and financial fines if they discuss what they've just described to the agents. (0:48:08)

And hence, you know, these people wait 20 and 30 years to talk to me or go public on their own as Bob Salas did and Bob Jacobs. They're concerned. Well, Jacobs wasn't interviewed, wasn't debriefed by OSI, but virtually all the other people who were that I've interviewed said, you know, they were so frightened at what essentially were threats about keeping your mouth shut that they waited decades to talk about this. (0:48:36)

So that does seem to be the pattern. I'm sure it's ongoing. I could mention this. People have asked me over the years, well, when you started researching or speaking publicly about your own work, were you threatened at all? Well, what happened to me was my first series of lectures was in the fall of 1981. I had, I believe, 16 dates at various colleges and universities around the upper Midwest. And at various schools in the audience were military veterans. (0:49:09)

They had read in the local newspaper that I was going to be speaking about all of this, and I showed up to listen to what I had to say. And at many of those schools, someone would come up to me and say, I'm a veteran. I was at such and such a base. This is what I did. And I know what you're talking about because the same thing happened to me or something similar. (0:49:27)

When that happened, I would ask all these individuals if they would be willing to sit for a formal interview at some point when I got off the road. Some said yes, some said no. But in February of 1982, I began a series of follow-up calls with, I think it was seven or eight of these individuals. (0:49:50)

And I would talk to them over the phone and, with their permission, record what they were telling me. After each one of those calls, I would hang up the phone, thank them for speaking with me, hang up the phone. Within a minute or two, I would get another call, pick up the phone, and no one was saying anything. All I heard was heavy breathing. And after about 30 seconds or a minute, they would hang up. (0:50:15)

And so the first time that happened, I went, okay, I'm on someone's radar. And I got frightened, frankly. I didn't know what was going to happen next. I was clearly pushing the envelope by discussing publicly classified information. Someone was not happy about that. I had gotten some national publicity through the United Press International Wire Service, which hundreds of newspapers around the country picked up this story about me talking about UFOs and a government cover-up. And apparently, I came to someone's attention. (0:50:51)

And so I sort of paused before I made the second call to the veteran. But I felt I was either going to do this or I wasn't. And I sort of just found the courage somewhere to keep at it, talk to these other individuals. But after every one of these calls, I had the same effect, same consequence where someone would call up. It was usually within five minutes. I think I recall once or twice, it was about an hour later. I got the same heavy breathing, no one talking into the phone call. So that's the kind of problems I've dealt with. (0:51:29)

Now, I know that I have an FBI file on me. In 2011, another researcher, he filed an FOI request on my behalf with the FBI to see if they had files on me. The letter that he got and subsequently forwarded to me, which I have, the FBI admitted that their master index showed that they did have files on me. And they claim when they look for them, they were missing. They further said there were other files at their headquarters in Washington, but they were undergoing transferring written files to digital files and they couldn't immediately provide them to me. (0:52:08)

So I know the FBI has files on me. I made similar inquiries with CIA and the National Security Agency. In those two cases I got, we can neither confirm nor deny responses. So I know my work has come to someone's attention and they're probably, even now that I'm not really researching much anymore, they're probably still keeping an eye on me. In fact, Jeff, as you may recall, we seem to have some communications issue earlier this year when you asked me to confirm this date to speak with you and I sent you a response. You did not get that response. (0:52:50)

Now, over the years, I have found when I'm speaking with sources, that is ex-military person, other researchers or journalists, I think what you're doing essentially is journalistic in this sense. I have these email problems. I have telephone problems. (0:53:07)

When I talk to those three categories of persons, more often than not, or at least as often as not, the phone calls get interrupted in midstream and I have to call them back and they call me back. And then there's ongoing email issues. So somebody's, you know, it's low level harassment. I think I know who's behind it, but I can't prove it. And, you know, I just view it. It comes with the territory. I don't lose any sleep over it. (0:53:35)

It doesn't stop you, which is important. But let me ask you one final question, Robert. I know you've had health problems in recent years and I understand you stopped doing the college lecture circuit, but you did decide, I gather, to continue your public activities. And I wonder if there's anything behind that motive at this stage in your life. I think I mentioned earlier, the last case that I investigated occurred in October 2010 at F.E. Warren Air Force Base in Wyoming. There was a large scale incident where five of these missile alert facilities, they're now called, the Air Force changed their name. They're no longer launch control facilities. They're now missile alert facilities. (0:54:24)

Anyway, in October, October 23rd of 2010, the Atlantic website had a dramatic story based on leaked information that five of these MAF's missile alert facilities suddenly could not communicate with F.E. Warren Air Force Base, meaning that if, God forbid, there had been an order to launch their missiles at that time, they could not have gotten their order through normal channels. It was subsequently learned that there was a backup airborne system that would have allowed them to launch their missiles if ordered to do so. (0:55:18)

But it was a major incident and a snafu. And as soon as I heard about that, I went, this probably is UFO related. And I spoke with an individual, I'm not going to identify him, who had contacts at F.E. Warren Air Force Base. And on my behalf, he approached these persons, and they were actually, these two missile maintenance technicians were out in the field addressing this communication issue. And both of them reported seeing what was described as a huge cigar-shaped object flying in the sky above the missile field when these technical issues were cropping up. So, as I suspected, there seemed to be a UFO link with all of that. (0:55:47)

But to do all of that, and to do it properly, requires a sort of a mental clarity that I don't think I have anymore, and a physical energy that I don't have anymore. So, after 2010, I more or less said, I'm a spectator from here on out. So, that's how I would describe myself at this point. But you feel comfortable sharing the earlier work that you did for so many years? (0:56:14)

Absolutely. Again, I have this driving sense that the public needs to know about this. This is real. I think the U.S. government does not have the right to keep us in the dark decade after decade about something as dramatic as UFOs shutting down or activating our nuclear weapons. (0:56:33)

And, you know, I don't expect to see in my lifetime the big announcement from some president saying, you know, all of this is true. They are from somewhere else. They've been here a long time. They've been interacting with us. And we've kept this all secret for years, for your own good, American public. And I don't think I'm going to live to see that. (0:56:53)

But there's been so many amazing things that have happened in the last five, six, seven years. ATIP coming out, Lou Elizondo in particular, he's confirmed in at least two interviews that I'm aware of in podcasts. He's confirmed that my work was right on. He said I gave information. I had information that ATIP used that they didn't have. And he's on camera saying all that. (0:57:20)

So I feel that, you know, belatedly, however later, however long it took to occur, people are finally starting to pay attention to the nuclear weapons link. Robert, from my point of view, you are a hero. You're doing an enormous public service. I don't know the price you may have paid for making that choice in your life. But I want to express on behalf of the New Thinking Allowed audience, certainly a lot of gratitude for what you've done and for the fact that in spite of being an abductee yourself, you've managed to maintain a level head. (0:57:59)

And you're very articulate about what you've experienced. I think that you are basically a credit to humanity. So thank you so much for being with me. Well, I have to respond to that. I would just say I was a stubborn guy who needed some answers. And whether or not there was an unseen guidance in what I did, again, that's up in the air. But, you know, when we get right down to it, the heroes, the people that deserve our praise and our thanks are the veterans who had the courage to speak to me and to come out. (0:58:31)

Even after some of them, many of them were told, you know, if you talk about this, you're going to be in deep trouble. Many of them waited decades, but they did finally come clean. And they're the ones that deserve the hero label, in my opinion. I can't disagree with that at all. You've been really the point of the spear, but there are a lot of people behind you carrying the spear as well. (0:58:57)

I understand. Thank you. Thank you so much for being with me. And for those of you watching or listening, thank you for being with us, because you are the reason that we are here.

entry.title: Dr. Gregory Rogers の証言 : 1992年に空軍基地の格納庫で UFO の動画映像を見た ⇒ この謎を推測する
entry.content:
前置き​

いわゆる UFO 目撃者の内部告発 動画のひとつ。

証言の核心部分は ここ にまとめた。

彼のこの証言の謎につての私の推測は ここ にまとめた。

情報源 : Youtube 動画(2:08:56)​

We Got It From Them-NASA Flight Surgeon's 1992 Cape Canaveral UFO Encounter

静止画​

AI

ロジャーズ博士: 目撃された空飛ぶ円盤

この音声記録は、ロジャーズ博士によるポッドキャストインタビューの一部で、ホストはクリス・レートです。

ロジャーズ博士は、1992年にケープカナベラルでUFOを目撃した体験を語っており、それは「空飛ぶ円盤」として詳細に描写されています。元NASAのフライトサージョンであり、F-16パイロットでもある彼の卓越した経歴と、その証言の信頼性が強調されています。

彼は、デビッド・グラッシュやフレイバー司令官といった他の証言者から影響を受け、引退後にこの体験を公表する準備ができたと述べています。

AI

詳細ブリーフィングドキュメント：UFO、脳損傷、航空の安全性、および政府の透明性

このブリーフィングドキュメントは、グレゴリー・ロジャース博士へのポッドキャストインタビューの抜粋をレビューし、以下の主要なテーマを強調します。

  1. ロジャース博士の未確認航空現象（UAP）目撃とそれを取り巻く状況

  • 1992年のUAP目撃: ロジャース博士は1992年、ケープカナベラルで「空飛ぶ円盤」を目撃したと証言しています。この出来事は彼のキャリアの中でわずか15分の出来事でしたが、彼の世界観を完全に変えました。彼は「米国空軍」の文字とアメリカの飛行機章が描かれた、縫い目や窓のない真珠のような白い楕円形の機体を目撃しました。機体は床から3フィートの高さまで浮上し、360度時計回りに回転し、その後反時計回りに回転し、左右、前後に移動しました。最も衝撃的だったのは、45度の迎角に移動しても「1センチメートルも動かなかった」ことです。これは従来の航空機の能力とは大きく異なります。彼はこの機体が「非人間的技術」によって製造されたと考えています。

  • 機密保持と情報開示: 目撃後、同僚の少佐から「誰にも見せたことを言わないでください」と忠告され、ロジャース博士は軍事における情報共有のリスクを認識したため、33年間この目撃について沈黙を守りました。彼は、「もし私がこの男を報告したら、彼らを報告しなければならないだろう」と述べ、自身のキャリアへの悪影響を懸念しました。しかし、デビッド・グラッシュやコマンダー・フレイバーのようなUAP目撃者の証言に触発され、引退後の2024年5月に公に語り始めました。彼の話は急速に広まり、世界中で注目を集めました。

  • 非人間的な技術とリバースエンジニアリング: ロジャース博士は、1992年に目撃した機体が「地球外からの非人間的な技術」に由来すると信じています。彼は、もし1947年以降に非人間の乗り物を回収していたとしても、その材料科学、高度なコンピューターシステム、および技術が人類にとって完全に未知であるため、リバースエンジニアリングには長い時間がかかるだろうと推測しています。彼は、2004年のティク・タクUAP（米海軍パイロットが目撃）も「本物であり、非人間的な知性によって制御されていた」と信じています。

  1. 航空における脳損傷：F-16パイロットと海軍SEALs

  • Gフォースと脳への影響: ロジャース博士は、F-18スーパーホーネットのパイロットや海軍SEALsが経験する繰り返しの衝撃やGフォースが、脳に深刻な損傷を与えるという懸念を表明しています。彼は「脳は濃いゼリーのような一貫性」を持っていると述べ、サッカー選手やアメリカンフットボール選手が頭をぶつけたり、爆発にさらされたりしたときに起こるのと同様に、航空機が極端なGフォース下で機動すると、脳が頭蓋骨の中で前後に揺れること（クー・アンド・コントレクー傷害）によって損傷を受けると説明しています。

  • 「プロジェクト・オーディンズ・アイ」と既存の知識: 米海軍が「プロジェクト・オーディンズ・アイ」という機密プロジェクトを立ち上げ、F-18スーパーホーネットのパイロットの脳機能に関する詳細なデータを収集して、極限飛行の累積的影響を評価していることについて、ロジャース博士は「この研究や調査は、何が起こっているかを私に伝える必要はない」と断言しています。彼は1980年代初頭に医学生だった頃から、これらの種類の脳損傷について知っていたと指摘しています。

  • 脳損傷の不可避性: ロジャース博士は、現在のところ人間の脳を変えることができない限り、Gフォースによる脳の揺れから保護するメカニズムはないと考えています。「頭蓋骨は固体です。頭蓋骨の片側を打つと、頭蓋骨の反対側は停止しますが、その間の脳は前後に跳ね返ります。」彼は、これにより多くのベテランパイロットが「若い頃のようにうまく考えられない」と訴え、頭痛などの症状を経験していると指摘しています。

  1. 飛行外科医の役割と航空安全文化

  • 飛行外科医の進化: ロジャース博士は、かつてはパイロットを飛行停止させることに熱心な「ジャーク」な飛行外科医もいたと述べていますが、自身のキャリアの後半には文化が変化し、飛行外科医が飛行隊に「統合され」、パイロットが安全に飛行できるよう「本当に興味を持つようになった」と感じています。

  • パイロットの健康管理の重要性: ロジャース博士は、パイロットの健康管理の重要性を強調するため、低血糖によって失神しかけたパイロットの事例を挙げ、その原因がサプリメントの摂取であったことを突き止め、最終的にパイロットを飛行任務に復帰させた経験を語っています。彼はまた、NASAで緑色のケミカルライトへの切り替えに1年半かかったという事例を挙げ、救助隊の視認性の重要性を訴えています。

  • 安全と管理の対立: ロジャース博士は、NASAのマネージャーが安全担当者のアドバイスを聞かず、スペースシャトルの修理キットを携行させなかったことなど、安全プロトコルが管理層によって無視される事例があったことを強く批判しています。彼は、コロンビア号の悲劇は、「NASAのマネージャーがマネージャーらしく行動し、安全担当者が言ったことに従わないことを選択した」ために起こったと示唆しています。

  • 飛行外科医の役割と経験: 飛行外科医は単なる医師ではなく、パイロットの仕事環境を完全に理解し、それに応じて医療上の決定を下す必要があると説明しています。彼はヘリコプターやF-16を操縦した経験があり、パイロットが直面する具体的な課題を理解していることが、彼らの健康と安全を守る上で不可欠であると強調しています。

  1. 政府の透明性と情報公開の必要性

  • 「何も見るものはない」という姿勢への批判: ロジャース博士は、政府がUAP情報について国民から隠蔽していることを、「ネイキッド・ガン」のフランク・ドレビン警部が「何も見るものはない」と言いながら背後で花火工場が爆発しているシーンになぞらえて批判しています。「それが私たちの政府がし続けていることです。」

  • 情報公開の動機: デビッド・グラッシュやコマンダー・フレイバーのような人々が情報公開に踏み切ったことに触発され、ロジャース博士も自身のUAP目撃談を公にしました。彼は、「さらに一人でも前に出て自分の真実の物語を語るたびに、フランク・ドレビンが『何も見るものはない』と言うのがますます難しくなる」と述べています。

  • 国家の秘密保持の戦略: ホストは、ポルトガルが新世界への航路を秘密にしたように、国家は常に技術的優位性を秘密にしてきた歴史を指摘しています。しかし、ホストは、この秘密主義が「長期的に実行可能な戦略であるとは思わない」と問いかけ、情報が「世界に本当に良い影響を与える」可能性がある場合、それを隠し続けることの倫理を疑問視しています。

  • 議会での証言への意欲: ロジャース博士は、議会で証言する意思があることを表明していますが、「もし議会の前に私を置くなら、私は自分が信じることを話します。だから、もし特定のことを言ってほしいなら、それは私ではありません。気にする必要はありません。もし行くなら、私は自分が思うことを話します。」

##結論

I trust you in every way except for speaking to the Secretary of Defense. On Wednesday morning, you've got a helicopter. You can fly anywhere you want in Germany. But you cannot return to base until I clear you too. Because if you are at the clinic, and the Secretary of Defense asks you a question, you're going to tell him what you think. (1:50:51)

And that is not advantageous for my purposes. So you've got a helicopter, fly anywhere you want. So I just flew around looking at castles all day. And then when the Secretary of Defense left, I came back and did my stuff. But he did not want me talking to the Secretary of Defense, because I would have told him exactly what I thought about a number of different issues. (1:51:17)

What was more fun than flying helicopters or the F-16? Helicopters. Yeah, I heard they're amazing to fly. Well, you can do all kinds of things in a helicopter. For instance, one time, we were supposed to be flying out on Route Yellow. And I was in an OH-58 with another pilot. And as we were getting to the entrance of Route Yellow, he said, hey, Doc, do you mind if we sort of deviate from course a little bit? And I said, well, maybe. What do you have in mind? He said, well, there's this large creek over here, and I'm a fisherman. (1:52:08)

But what I'd like to do, if you don't mind, is sort of go down that place and look for a good fishing hole. So I said, well, okay, we can do it. So I was at the controls. So I took us over. And so we went into a little 15-foot hover and just sort of working our way down this creek. (1:52:28)

And as we go around this one bend, there's this German guy that's fishing. And so the other pilot, you have a knee pad, and you can ride on it. He said, okay, yeah, let's check that guy out. And so he motioned to him. And so the guy lifted his stringer, and he's got all this fish on it. (1:52:50)

So he said, okay, this is what I want. Go up to about 25 feet and follow that road he's on. And let's see where it goes. So he made himself a map while I was flying us over. And then when we got to the main road, he said, there's a little town that way. (1:53:09)

And so I flew us over to where we could see the the name of the little town. And so he said, okay, I've got my map. Let's go back to yellow. So we went back to yellow and off we go. One time I was in a Huey and we were flying along and we were doing nap of the earth, which means we did not want to be more than 10 feet above the ground at any point. (1:53:38)

If there was a tree or mountain sticking up, we went around the tree, not over the tree. So we're flying along. It's a summer day and the doors are open in the cargo area. And as we went across this field of yellow flowers, all of a sudden the rotor wash picked up the smell of these flowers and just engulfed us. (1:54:00)

We couldn't smell the JP4. We couldn't smell hydraulics. All we could smell was these flowers. So we're all looking at each other. (1:54:04)

Hey, do you smell that? Yeah. And so when we got to the other edge and we left the flowers behind within a few seconds, here's all the JP4 smell, the hydraulics and all that kind of stuff. But for like 20 seconds, all we could smell were these flowers. And so it's something that stands out in my mind. Yeah, you can't do either of those things in an F-16. I guess you could if you used a targeting pod. You could see if the guy was catching a fish. (1:54:50)

You actually could see if there was fish on his line. Then you could track the road back. So I guess you could do that. It'd be a lot more difficult. But I guess it's possible if the trees... Yeah, especially with the speed that the Viper would be moving. It took me four or five minutes in the helicopter to note all of the stuff because the road went back and there was a fork coming off. (1:55:17)

So he had to mark, not this fork, go this way. And so he not only made the map, but he had to give himself instructions for how to follow the map. Excellent. Well, thanks again, Greg, Dr. Rogers, and for your book. I hope that we see it in the future. And if it's not self-published that another publisher picks it up, but I'd recommend everyone in the audience to check it out. (1:55:49)

So Impact by Dr. Gregory Rogers, and I wish they took your advice back then. And hopefully they'll take your advice now and come clean and start sharing this information with the public. Yeah. Well, let me give you another example. When I got to Kennedy Space Center, in the left lower leg pocket of the astronauts, they had two chemlights. (1:56:17)

And so if they bailed out into the Atlantic ocean, they were supposed to pick up these chemlights and show them to us in the dark. Well, they were red chemlights. Our night vision goggles couldn't see them unless we were really close to them. Now then, if you had green chemlights, we could see them from five miles away. (1:56:35)

It took a year and a half for me to convince NASA to switch to green chemlights because they said, well, it might ruin the vision of the astronaut. I said, I don't care about the astronaut. I care about my vision and the vision of my crew. We cannot save them if we don't see them. Our vision is most important. If we see the green chemlight, we know where to go save that astronaut. (1:57:04)

It took a year and a half for me to convince them to switch to green chemlights. Also, green doesn't ruin your night vision anyway. I mean, that's why we use green lights in the cockpit of the F-16. It's our enviz. Well, by the time we're hovering over them, we're going to have our own lights. So lighting is not going to be an issue if we can identify this is where we need to do a lift and save this astronaut's life. We'll have our own lights and they're going to be brighter than the chemlights. (1:57:41)

But the most important thing is we have to locate the astronauts before we can save them. (1:57:50)

So my purpose was to save the lives of the astronauts, not play political games with the NASA managers. Okay, well, thank you, Dr. Rogers. And thank you so much for being on the show and for chatting. It's been a true pleasure and I hope we can stay in contact. I'd like to send the prompt to get you to describe, actually, in as many words as you can. (1:58:23)

And we can use some AI artwork to see if we can get a better rendition of the craft, make it as accurate as possible, if you'd be willing to help me with that. Excellent. So I'll be showing that through the interview. Not a problem. Amazing. Okay. Thank you, sir. Okay, well, thank you. And I thank you for your service. People say that in general. (1:58:48)

People say that in general. But, you know, there's no way they know everything that we have to go through to serve our country, especially when you're doing something as dangerous as flying an F-16. The average person out there cannot imagine everything you went through with flight training and night navigation and all the different things. I can't imagine it. It's just kind of like a dream, like another life. (1:59:26)

But it's paid off. I have relatively minimal issues. And I'm here, you know, a lot of my friends didn't make it, actually. So I try and do my best and live. I try and live with integrity and do right, but what I think is correct, not by, you know, what other people... Well, even with peacetime aircraft mishaps, I had to go pick up parts of what used to be my friends. (1:59:56)

Now, then the average person out there never has to do anything like that. So they can't relate to it. Well, I hope they listen. Would you consider going to, talking to Congress, talk to any congressional members? I've been asked that question, especially while I was out at contact in the desert, and I said that I would. (2:00:36)

But the caveat is just like with the Secretary of Defense. If you put me in front of Congress, I'm going to tell what I believe. So if you're wanting someone to say any particular things, that's not me. Don't even bother. If I go, I'm going to tell what I think. Well, perfect. Well, I hope you go, sir. I really do. That would be amazing. (2:01:11)

So anyone watching, please, let's try and make this happen. Okay, well, thank you so much. I really appreciate being here. And I enjoyed talking to you. So, you know, these days, even though I work at the McAllister Army ammunition plant for 14 years prior to retiring, there were not a lot of people out there that really knew the tactical aviation world or the space launch world or anything like that. (2:01:40)

So when I get a chance to talk to somebody who speaks the same language, so to speak, it's always a pleasure. And I remember back fondly with the flight surgeons we had, you know, and they completely helped me and my wife and my family. So I think, you know, you guys make a real impact. So I want to thank flight surgeons and all the ones that helped us really did over the years. Well, that's what we're supposed to do. (2:02:10)

If we're not doing it, there's something wrong. Yeah, they definitely did. No, we had amazing flight surgeons. So no, I want to thank you for your service, man, for helping everybody you did and continuing to do now. So yeah, it's really impressive and motivating. It makes it, you know, a pleasure to do this job, really makes it rewarding to do this, you know, get a lot of troll comments. (2:02:41)

And, you know, it's difficult coming out and speaking about this topic. You know, I could easily be making videos about the war. I could be talking about the weapons and the fighting and everything and getting way more views. But I, you know, I think this is much more meaningful. So I think history will show that you're doing the right thing and that it's going to be the honorable thing in the end. So thank you again. (2:03:00)

Well, thank you. I appreciate being on your show. (2:03:04)

I don't know if you could tell during that interview, but I really was blown away. By his story. And then just chatting with him over a few hours and the email we had beforehand. I just felt this special bond, just like I was back in a fighter squadron. And you know, the flight surgeon flies with you in your squadron. (2:03:30)

And he's your friend, you know, you fly with them all the time, they'll fly in the back seat. And then when you go to get checks, when you go to get help, you know, you have issues with your family, issues with your kids. You know, I remember Doc Smith, amazing flight surgeon I had. He had incredible stories that I won't share here. (2:03:51)

But I remember him helping my family when my wife was pregnant, you know, and really helping us. And you just feel like you have this friend, a great close friend who is a doctor. That's what I would say a flight surgeon is. And that's really what they got to. And as we talked about with Dr. Rogers, early in the day, he had met that one doctor who knocked he kept track of the pilots that he had denift, which is removed from flying permanently, not denift, but removed from flying permanently. (2:04:19)

And I think that was the previous days. And also we didn't try and make our doctors puke, you know, I never did that. Plus, you're sitting in a cockpit with someone who just puked, it's super gross. So I actually flew smooth. And most of the time, it didn't even matter. They would still puke, not the doctors, doctors would get used to it. And the story was amazing. (2:04:40)

I didn't ask him during the interview, how large was the craft, but afterwards, it was 20 feet long, he said, and about 10 feet tall. And then he worked with my AI designer, thank you to Colin Stone, amazing designer, does my thumbnails as well. And he was able to create those renders that you see throughout the video. And yeah, it seems like the sports model, Bob Lazar came out in, what, 89. So this was three years after. (2:05:06)

What are the chances that they could have made this craft in that time? You know, it seems like it's a perfect alignment with Bob Lazar's story. And the electrostatic effects, I hadn't heard that before. I do remember the amazing electrostatic UFO that was up in Canada, right, with the defense contractor saw. (2:05:30)

And that's really the first time I seriously started considering that these are electrostatic machines that actually use, obviously, electromagnetic energy, which we understand is one form of that is light. But light is electric and magnetic. And so, yeah, these craft use some sort of advanced technology able to bend what we understand of as gravity, which I believe is the interaction of light and matter. (2:05:55)

And again, we don't really know what matter is. We just know that light interacts with it. And so, we still have a lot to learn. (2:06:01)

But I think this is just deep insight into the program that I think exists, and seems to obviously exist inside the animal that is the military industrial complex of the United States. And the question is, when will this information come out? You know, it will come out sooner or later. At some point in the future, we'll find out about this. (2:06:24)

Just remember, nations have always done this in the past, right? There's no way Spain or Portugal ever shared how they traveled to the New World. You know, Portugal had a way to go around the southern tip of Africa. And there's no way in hell they shared that with any of their adversaries, right? And they became the richest, most powerful country in Europe. And they were a tiny little nation, if you think about that. (2:06:47)

And that's really through information and technological superiority, right? Their ships and their cannons, and they had the information and the adventurous spirit to go way far west, hitting Brazil, and that swooped them around the southern tip of Africa. And so they were able to enter a new world with information and technology. And there is no way in hell they shared that information, right? But we know it now, right? Looking back in the past, we know what happened. (2:07:14)

So this is not something new. Nations have always done this. Why would we expect them to be any different? Why would we expect the United States to be any different from all the nations of the past? So I think this program will come out, but it will take courageous people with integrity, like Dr. Rogers, speaking out on these topics. (2:07:36)

And you saw he was motivated by David Grush and Commander Fravor. And I am excited to hear of anyone motivated by Dr. Rogers. And I would say, go and do it, right? What is your life going to mean at the end anyway, if you're going to die with this secret that is information that could really affect the world? And I believe in a positive way, right? The world is in a terrible hurt right now. (2:07:58)

We're on the brink of World War Three, if you will. And something's got to change. And this idea of just keeping everything secret, just so your nation can pull further ahead of the other nations, I don't think is a long-term, viable strategy. And all nations perish, right? Every nation will perish. It's just a matter of time, like you will perish. (2:08:20)

So what is your memory going to be? What are people going to remember you for? And what are people going to remember our nations for? The nation of the United States, will it be remembered as keeping this information secret from humanity forever, like the Portuguese did, just to gain a national advantage? So we'll see. So if you want to support the channel, please do subscribe to get future notifications. (2:08:41)

And you can support the channel further at patreon.com forward slash Chris Slato or become a YouTube member. It does really help. (2:08:47)

You can join the likes of these amazing people. Thanks again for your support and for watching. Have a great rest of your day. Peace. (2:08:55)

(2025-06-30)

entry.title: 1947-07-06, Maryland : 傘型の UFO ⇒ この謎を推測
entry.content:
前置き​

比較的珍しい形状の UFO 目撃事例。目撃者がその場で描いたスケッチがある。

Case 306 -- July 5, Bethesda, Maryland: Jack LaBous, a Washington artist living in the 3500 block of East Capital Street, was riding on a Benning bus near Bethesda sometime during the morning when he saw a flat, disc-shaped object with a small dome-like shape on the underside, spinning high in the air at an altitude he estimated to be above 15,000 feet. He also noticed a stick-like appendage, like a radio antenna, protruding downward from the center under the object (see drawing).

Mr. LaBous worked for eight years as a visual artist for the Civil Aeronautics Administration; when he saw the object, he quickly made a sketch of it on the back of an envelope he had in his pocket. The detail of the "antenna-like" appendage is remarkably similar to the device described by Gregory Zimmer in Sioux Falls the following day (Case 452).

Case 306 - - July 5

Bethesda, Md.

From sketch by witness

ケース306 -- 7月5日、メリーランド州ベセスダ：ワシントン在住のアーティスト、ジャック・ラボウス氏は、ベセスダ近郊のイースト・キャピタル・ストリート3500番街区在住で、朝のある時間帯にベニング行きのバスに乗っていたところ、高度約15,000フィート上空を高速で回転する平らな円盤状の物体を見ました。その物体の下部に小さなドーム状の形状が確認されました。また、物体の中心部から下方に突き出た棒状の突起物（ラジオアンテナのような形状）にも気づきました（図参照）。

ラボス氏は、民間航空局（CAA）の視覚アーティストとして8年間勤務していました。物体を目撃した際、ポケットに入れていた封筒の裏に素早くスケッチを描きました。この「アンテナのような突起」の詳細は、翌日にスーフォールズでグレゴリー・ジンマーが報告した装置（ケース452）と驚くほど類似しています。

ref: http://kirkmcd.princeton.edu/JEMcDonald/bloecher_67.pdf

コメント​

高度の見積もりが 5000m なので、サイズもそれなりに大きいはず。

推測だが、潰れた観測気球が周囲の気流に力によって傘の形状に潰れて回転していたのではないか。

下部が潰れたから、

その物体の下部に小さなドーム状の形状が確認されました。

として見えたと。なお、この当時、幾つもの観測気球が飛ばされていた記録がある。

(2025-06-30)

entry.title: John Greenewald, Jr. : WSJ の UFO 記事を強く批判
entry.content:
前置き​

John Greenewald, Jr. が WSJ の UFO 記事（有料）を強く批判している。

関連​

この WSJ の有料記事については下の過去記事でも扱った。

Richard Dolan の批判 : WSJ が UFO 情報撹乱工作を仕掛けてきた (2025-06-17)

AI

音声対話​

https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/bb6a8c31-8819-4c43-b799-8f58ff64266d/audio

情報源 : Youtube 動画(1:26:30)​

The Wall Street Journal Covers UAP - My Take

AI

ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナルUFO記事の検証​

このソースは、ジョン・グリーンウォルド・ジュニア氏によるYouTubeポッドキャストの文字起こしで、ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナル紙のUAP（未確認航空現象）に関する記事を検証しています。

彼は、ジャーナリズムにおける情報の省略と、それがどのように誤解を招くかについて論じています。グリーンウォルド氏は、自身の広範な情報提供が記事に反映されなかったことに対する不満を表明し、ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナル紙が特定の政府のディスインフォメーションの物語に焦点を当て、UAPに関する分類された文書の豊富な歴史を無視したと主張しています。

彼は、根拠のない主張を盲目的に信じることに対する批判を展開し、完全な証拠に基づく分析の必要性を強調しています。

AI

ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナルUFO記事の検証：

主要テーマと重要な事実の要約​

ジョン・グリーンウォルド・ジュニアによるこのYouTubeポッドキャストは、ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナル（WSJ）のUAP（未確認航空現象）に関する2部構成の記事を検証し、その主要なテーマ、主張、そしてグリーンウォルド氏がWSJに提供した情報がなぜ記事に採用されなかったのかについて深く掘り下げています。グリーンウォルド氏は、WSJの記事がUAP現象に関する誤報と情報の限定的な側面を強調しすぎていると批判しています。

  1. WSJ記事の主題とグリーンウォルド氏の主な批判点

WSJの記事は、UAP現象の多くが政府の極秘技術の隠蔽や、意図的な誤情報・偽情報キャンペーンの結果であるという見解を提示しています。特に、エリア51周辺でのUFO神話の拡散が、政府によるトップシークレット技術の隠蔽目的で行われたという「空軍大佐がバーでUFO写真を仕掛けた」という噂を取り上げています。

グリーンウォルド氏の主要な批判は以下の通りです。

  • 証拠の欠如と限定的な視点: WSJの記事は「誤情報と偽情報、この話題には何も関係ない」という印象を与えていますが、その主張を裏付ける具体的な情報源や証拠に欠けています。記事は特定の個人からの証言に依存しており、「信頼できる兄弟」の物語と同じレベルで、証拠がないとグリーンウォルド氏は指摘します。

  • 重要な情報の省略: グリーンウォルド氏は、自身がWSJに提供した数時間にもわたるインタビューと膨大な文書（FOIAを通じて入手した数千ページの政府文書を含む）が、記事に一切使用されなかったことを強く批判しています。これらの文書は、UFO/UAPが依然として高度に機密化されており、長年にわたって世界中で遭遇が記録されていることを示しています。もしこれが単に政府のトップシークレット技術であれば、多くの情報が半世紀以上も機密化されたまま存在し続けることは考えにくいと主張しています。

  • 軍事技術との区別: B-2ステルス爆撃機やF-117ステルス戦闘機のようなかつて極秘だった軍事技術でさえ、数十年後には一般に公開され、航空ショーなどで見られるようになっているにもかかわらず、UAP関連文書が今なお高度に機密化されていることは、それが既知の軍事技術ではない可能性を示唆していると述べています。

  1. WSJ記事が取り上げた具体的なテーマとグリーンウォルド氏の反論 WSJ記事が焦点を当てたいくつかの具体的なテーマに対し、グリーンウォルド氏は反論を提示しています。

  • 「ヤンキー・ブルー」ハラスメントの儀式: WSJは、ペンタゴンが2023年に「ヤンキー・ブルー」と呼ばれるハラスメントの儀式を発見し、これにより人々がエイリアン技術に関わる極秘プログラムに参加していると誤解させられたと報じました。しかし、グリーンウォルド氏がAFOSI（空軍特別捜査局）に提出したFOIA請求では、2021年以降に「ヤンキー・ブルー」に関連する調査の記録は一切見つかりませんでした。

  • ロバート・サラス氏の証言とEMPテスト: WSJは、ロバート・サラス氏が主張する1967年のミサイルシャットダウン事件について、EMP（電磁パルス）テストが原因である可能性を示唆する文書のスクリーンショットを掲載しました。しかし、WSJは関連する文書全体を公開せず、グリーンウォルド氏は、この文書がサラス氏の体験全体を否定するものではないと指摘しました。また、サラス氏の事例以外にも、核施設や軍事基地へのUFOの侵入が多数報告されており、これらもWSJの記事では無視されていると批判しています。

  • ルイ・エリゾンド氏と「To the Stars Academy」: WSJの記事のパート2は、ルイ・エリゾンド氏と「To the Stars Academy of Arts and Science」に焦点を当てていましたが、グリーンウォルド氏はこれを「昔のニュースの焼き直し」と評しました。

  1. 省略された重要な情報源と文書

グリーンウォルド氏は、WSJに提供したにもかかわらず記事で省略された重要な情報源や文書をいくつか挙げています。

  • CIAのUFO関連文書: 政府がUFO調査を終了したと主張した後も、CIAがUFO/UAP問題を監視し続けていたことを示す文書。

  • UAPタスクフォースによるNASAへのブリーフィング資料: UAPがいかに高度に機密化されているかを示すもので、一部が黒塗りされており、全てのUAPの選択肢すら開示されていない。

  • UAP関連の写真・動画の機密扱い: ロシアのジェット機による無人機への燃料噴射の映像が速やかに公開される一方で、UAP関連の全ての画像は100%機密扱いされている現状。政府は「能力」の開示を理由にしていますが、グリーンウォルド氏はこれを「馬鹿げている」と一蹴しています。

  • UAPセキュリティ分類ガイド: UAP情報の機密性を定義する文書で、これがUAPが単なる既知の軍事技術ではないことを示唆していると主張。

  • 国家安全保障局（NSA）および国防情報局（DIA）のUFO関連ファイルの紛失: これらの機関が多数のUFO関連ファイルを「謎の紛失」としており、これは情報隠蔽の可能性を示唆しています。

  • OSAPプログラムに関する誤解: DIAのOSAP（高度航空宇宙脅威識別プログラム）の真のミッションと、それが「スキンウォーカー牧場でのダイナビーバー狩り」のような逸話と混同されていることへの批判。グリーンウォルド氏は、これによりUAP研究全体の信頼性が損なわれていると懸念しています。

  1. メディアと一般への提言

ピーター・ジェニングスに対する第三者からの主な批判は以下の通りです。

  • 経験不足と「グラマーキャスター」としての批判: キャリアの初期、ABCニュースのアンカーに抜擢された際、経験不足であると批判されました。特に、彼のカナダなまりの英語（例：「lieutenant」を「leftenant」と発音する）や、アメリカの文化や情勢に関する知識の不足から、「グラマーキャスター（見かけ倒しのキャスター）」と揶揄されることもありました。

  • 中東報道における偏向の疑惑: ベイルート支局長時代には、アラブ・イスラエル紛争においてアラブ側に肩入れしているという批判を受けました。特に、1972年のミュンヘンオリンピック事件の報道では、黒い9月（ブラック・セプテンバー）のメンバーを「テロリスト」ではなく「ゲリラ」や「コマンドー」と表現したことに対して批判がありました。また、イスラエルに対する偏見があるという指摘も長年にわたってなされており、パレスチナ側の暴力に言い訳を与えている、あるいはイスラエルとパレスチナの行動に道徳的な同等性があるかのように示唆している、といった批判がありました。

  • 銃規制に関する誤報: 銃規制に関する報道において、誤った情報を提供したとして批判されたことがあります。例えば、特定の銃器が「アサルトウェポン」であると誤って報じたり、銃規制法が施行される前の事件にその法律が適用されるかのように示唆したりしたことに対し、正確性を欠いていると指摘されました。

  • 政治的偏見の疑惑: 1994年の議会選挙で共和党が全国的に勝利した際、「有権者はかんしゃくを起こした」という発言をしたことが、彼の政治的偏見を示していると解釈され、批判を浴びました。

これらの批判は、彼のジャーナリズムの客観性や正確性、そして特定の政治的・社会的問題に対するスタンスに向けられたものでした。

This included all the CIA material that I made reference to, where UAP material was in the halls of the CIA, that they were still looking in to the UFO and UAP issue and phenomena. (0:54:30)

Now, if we're dealing with primarily top-secret tech and Blue Force technology and stuff that's readily identifiable, maybe not to the pilot who saw it, but to the U.S. military that's getting the report and it goes up the chain a little bit. And they go, yeah, we can't tell Sergeant so-and-so that this is what they saw. But yeah, this has been tested for a little bit. We got it stationed out in wherever. (0:55:10)

The Wall Street Journal, by the way, completely ignored all of this. (0:58:27)

They did deal with the TTSA CRADA, but I did send that on. (0:58:52)

I believe that I was the first site to publish this when it first came out. It was very important to see. The UAP security classification guide, same deal. I did find, and still find, Luis Elizondo's confirmed position, the director of what's called the NPSMS, what they did. (0:59:11)

And I talked about how, like through FOIA, when it says our mission, this was actually written by the director of the NPSMS after Elizondo had retired, and they said the mission relates strictly to, and then they wouldn't say what. In my opinion, that says SAPS, S-A-P-S, Special Access Programs. I can't confirm that, obviously, because it's redacted, but I do believe the NPSMS does deal with SAP access. (0:59:37)

I went into details about that. Clearly, the Wall Street Journal didn't talk about this aspect of the story, and, you know, maybe that just wasn't their angle, and I can... that's fine, whatever, I'm not going to harp on them for that. But it is a very interesting story, nonetheless. The OSAP documentation, obviously, OSAP coming up. There is a huge differentiation, if you ask me, between the DIA's mandated OSAP mission, and what they essentially contracted out, and what Bigelow Aerospace's subsidiary BAS, the contractor for OSAP, actually did. (1:00:16)

I believe that there is a huge gap, and a huge separation. I think it is a fantastic story. I think a lot of it is not written yet, but I do not believe the Skinwalkers at the Pentagon aspect to all of this is what the DIA wanted. And I believe that that is very important. (1:00:53)

Because in the process of all of this, a lot of those skeptical-minded people that are constantly bashing this whole topic, they kind of connect the quote-unquote government's program, OSAP, to chasing dino beavers at a ranch in Utah. And they kind of put it all together, and say, see, this is all just stupid, and the government's dumb for investigating it, because all it is is rooting to these people who run around looking for werewolves and dino beavers and chasing ghosts. (1:01:09)

Now, I'm not here to talk about dino beavers and werewolves and ghosts. Maybe they exist, who knows. But my point is, is that you can't conflate the two missions. And I think that you have a lot of money that maybe was just private sector money, and they piggybacked on to some taxpayer-funded program known as OSAP. Or maybe there's some misappropriation of funds, but obviously that gets pretty dicey. (1:01:38)

Nobody wants to talk about that. But that is also a, and I stress the word possibility, that funds were not managed and spent appropriately within the DIA. So the DIA signs off on a program that we all know as OSAP, a forward-looking, 40-years-into-the-future technology program, what can we learn about propulsion X, Y, and Z. And then that's spun off into, let's go to Skinwalker Ranch and hunt the dino beaver. There's a lot of questions there that a lot of people aren't asking. But it's a very, very crucial differentiation, because I think you do have a true mission on the side of the U.S. government to figure out what these phenomena are, and that. (1:02:24)

And I don't believe they're one and the same. Others try and push them together, and I think the one side, that dino beaver side, cheapens the other. And as a result, the general public goes, yeah, just a bunch of crazy people looking for dino beavers. It's stupid. And they just kind of dismiss it. And I'm sorry, that's kind of the generalized outlook that people have on this topic. (1:02:50)

Because if that's what they're confronted with, with tabloid-style journalism from New York Post and this type of stuff, lazy journalism from Wall Street Journal, then they kind of just, in their mind, because they're not like you and I, where they're watching videos and stuff like that, they just shove it all together and go, yeah, it's just a bunch of crazy stuff. And that's why I get frustrated, because you have to separate the two. And you look at what Arrow did, and this may not even be to their fault, but a lot of their focus was the OSAP stuff, the looking at Skinwalker Ranch, that type of funding, the people that were involved in that, that those really outlandish stories all kind of root to the same couple of people. (1:03:34)

I think they called it a core group of people. And that is absolutely true. So you take the pie, which is the truth, you take one piece of it out, and you take a bite and put the bite on the side. The Wall Street Journal and Arrow both are looking at that one little bite and think they know everything about the pie. I've never been on the PSYOP bandwagon, but maybe that's the point. They love the Wall Street Journal saying goodbye to the verifiable evidence, to the documentation, to the claims that can actually be backed up with evidence. But if they do, it'll be like on page 9 with font 2 and just like you could barely read it. That's going to be their correction. So it's one of the two. And their online version, which then at that point no one will be reading, that's if you even want to choose to pay them to get past the big old fat paywall, it'll just be in a font size negative 2 at the bottom. And you read this whole article and they say, oh, correction. We X, Y, Z. We regret the error and that's it. But it's made six months after the fact and who really cares? Like nine people will see it and a few people will post it on social media, but nobody cares. The damage is done. (1:06:38)

So it seems like people want that. (1:06:41)

Moving on on some of the links that I sent them. Jay Stratton came up. I'm using Twitter screenshots just so you can see them. But the link doesn't show on this one. But Travis Taylor as well, I had sent over. I also sent them specifically the DIA records and the CIA ones. Those were records I showed you earlier in the visuals here. There was a reason for that. And again, with any journalists that I talk to, with you guys as well, if I'm on a live stream or if I'm doing my own written articles, if I make a claim, I do my darndest to cite it and give you a documented piece of information. (1:08:49)

A piece of evidence to go along with it. If it's an opinion of some kind, then I try and tell you that as well. If it was a 10-minute conversation, that's fine. But if you waste hours of somebody's time and you're getting paid and they're not, have the decency to respect the topic you're covering. Let alone the respect to the person who's spent hours of their time with you. That aside, give the topic the respect. If you're covering something and you're trying to get background on something, respect people's time and respect the information that you're getting and respect the topic that you're covering because people are relying on you to tell them the truth. (1:10:25)

And that's what's weird about all of this because when you go back to the original slide that I showed you and how I was pitched what this Wall Street Journal article was, was it that? I'll take your questions. (1:11:23)

I've got a couple minutes before I have to go pick up my son here. But I think that that's what I hope journalists in the future understand. But more than that, that's what I want you guys to understand and people around you, if you help spread that word, that just because the Wall Street Journal is the masthead, that that's the logo at the top of an article, that means absolutely nothing about the truth of that article. (1:12:20)

About what's going on with UAP and how there's nothing to the topic and it's all stories and this and that. All right, so let me see if there's any questions here. (1:13:29)

I say that respectfully because, again, I really do like Tim Burchett. And sadly, I think he's being misled by people I think he thinks are trustworthy. And that's unfortunate, but I say that with all due respect. (1:15:07)

So that being said, I do appreciate your support of the channel. So thank you for that. All right. Let me get to this one here. BrianStory8128, thank you for that. Thanks from the community. We are here with you and appreciate your efforts. Thank you so much, Brian. Really do appreciate that. Definitely means a lot to me. So let me go back to the normal chat. (1:15:43)

Again, I will see any comments that I can here. All caps really helps. I don't have moderators. You're looking at the entire staff of the Black Vault. HyperSonicT6W, John, what do you think of Jake Barber's claims? Okay. So, I mean, this is a video in itself. And I think Jake Barber fits in that category. I believe that the video that was released that was connected to him of the egg was... I don't know what the right word is to me, but it was pretty wonky. (1:16:12)

It just something seems very off to me. I don't dismiss it just because I have a gut feeling. So don't take that the wrong way. But rather, look, when you look at the video, it just doesn't seem right. And I feel that if it really did show something extraordinary, we would have had a lot happen since then. And we haven't. And I think a lot of these things are said for hype. I think a lot of these things are done for clicks. And that doesn't necessarily mean the root of the video is. But rather, he did so and got entangled with people that said, hey, let me put you on a news program. Let me write an article about you. All of that is great, but we need the evidence. We need to focus on the evidence. And that's great that they really want to help, but it's like, okay, we don't need more of that. It's just the same. Let's move beyond it. In 30 years, near 30 years, I can tell you I have seen so many UFO organizations, especially through the .com craze. (1:18:07)

You know, what is that, like the early 2000s and mid 2000s? UFO focused .coms. You see a lot of high price tags for membership fees, but they're not sharing any of the information. It's okay. I feel any way that it's okay. If an organization collects money, not a problem. And it's the age-old story, and it just gets tweaked over time. But again, the .coms of the early 2000s to, you know, all these UFO research organizations and efforts today, it's all the same to me, sadly, which is a shame. (1:19:39)

John, what do you think about the latest claims of summoning UAPs? Again, if you can summon UAPs, you shouldn't charge people to go out and teach them how to do it. It should be collective knowledge that you change humanity with, and you'll sell a billion copies of your book. Or there's like a, you know, select group of people that they'll take out in private to show. Sadly, you also got the Chris Bledsoe's of the world and him included. I will get hate mail for saying this. Chris genuinely strikes me as someone who I thought was genuine. I used to think that. I think maybe my feelings are changing a little bit. But he always struck me as someone who was genuine, that was misidentifying stuff in the sky. (1:20:51)

Now, it has turned very cult-like. I'm sorry, but it just has. And you look at the information that's coming out, people seeing these UFOs, quote-unquote UFOs that are with him, that are like satellites. Like, you don't... I live in North Los Angeles County. It gets pretty dark up here. I can go out any single night and see UFOs, excuse me, see satellites that some people equate as UFOs, but they're satellites. (1:21:18)

There's apps to help you track. There's historical data you can reference. And you see that with the Bledsoe material. And he just turns a blind eye to it. (1:21:52)

That, as a dad, was absolutely heart-wrenching to hear because you're utilizing the pain of somebody and connecting that to a SpaceX launch. But in his mind, and how he was conveying it over the phone, was this was a craft from somewhere beyond. This was a sign from the heavens. And it ultimately, if you turn the volume down, super cool video of a SpaceX launch and then a meteorite came in. And you see that in the video, super cool. But you turn the audio up and you go, yeah, let's not. That changed my mind on a lot of stuff, which is unfortunate. But I'm sorry. If you're mistaken, I believe that that's forgivable. (1:22:34)

You should want to know more. You should keep asking questions. If you look up, you see an airplane, you take a photo of it, you post and go, oh, I saw a UFO, but you were genuinely thinking it was unidentified, that's okay. You're not going to get grief from me. But if somebody points out definitively it was an aircraft, don't freak out and don't take offense to that. And those that take offense to these cases being solved shows how much they really, really want to know. (1:23:03)

I've only got time for maybe one more. Grant, always a pleasure seeing you. Hey, John, always good to see you. Did you happen to catch the Timothy Phillips interview? So what are your thoughts on Arrow's seemingly close relationship with the FBI and the use of B7? (1:23:17)

Yes. So the short of it, Grant, and that's an excellent question, is I have talked about the B7 connection for a long time. They've utilized that for a long time. They cannot name the law enforcement reasoning that they're using behind it. And if they have a connection with the FBI, which is fine, the FBI can only utilize, or FBI information can only have the B7 exemption utilized if there's an active and current law enforcement investigation or it kind of blows their law enforcement techniques. (1:23:52)

Other than that, you can't. Now, you can't just blanket everything with B7. Even if Arrow was an investigative agency, which I've argued legally, even if they were, you can't do these blanket denials, which they have. So if I'm understanding your question correctly, you know, is that connection with the FBI may be playing a role in the B7? Possibly, but it's Arrow's mandate, not the FBI's. And the FBI, I would almost guarantee, is not involved with every aspect of information that Arrow gets. Or we just wouldn't have an Arrow. I mean, plain and simple. (1:24:34)

So the fact that Arrow is blanket denying what they are, I believe is still not legally justifiable, even if the FBI is playing a role. That's if you ask me. Those are my two cents. So, Grant, like I said, always thank you so much for that. Let me do one more resolute decide. Yeah, where you been, man? Sorry. Listen to the beginning if you didn't hear it, but I do apologize of my absence. I've missed the one grounded voice in this field. Any future content I can look forward to? Yes, and that's a great closing note. (1:25:12)

At this point, since I am done with the kind of family obligation of moving my mom, very happy I'm done there. So a lot of that free time I will be able to, not that there is much free time, but I'm definitely in more of a position to be able to flip the camera on, sweat under the lights here and talk to all of you guys. So I look forward to that. (1:25:35)

Anyway, thank you guys. I really do appreciate it. Always a blast to hang out with you and talk a little bit about what I've been doing. I've written a ton of stories on TheBlackVault.com, so please make sure you take a look at that and see what you're maybe missing because I don't have time to do videos on everything. But I will try and bring more to you guys, so definitely take a look at those recent articles, and there are more to come. That's not a coming soon tease. You know I'll deliver on that one. Anyway, thank you guys. Truly appreciate it. We'll see you next time. (1:26:11)

entry.title: 1947-06-21, Maury Island UFO 事件の捏造説
entry.content:
前置き​

過去記事、

1947-06-21, Maury_Island 事件 : UFO 目撃は捏造、B-25 が墜落したのは偶発…という説 (2022-10-05)

に関連して、より詳細な捏造説を取り上げる。別記事の一部だが、別記事の情報源が長大なので埋もれている。そこで該当箇所をピンポイントで示しておく。

詳細データ​

Maury_Island 事件の捏造説

コメント​

この捏造を行った Fred Crisman は J.F.K. 暗殺事件でも登場している。この捏造が元で政府職員が死亡し起訴されかけた。その起訴をれるために諜報機関と司法取引をした可能性がある。それにより、後に組織された CIA の手駒となり、J.F.K. 暗殺に加担したと。

おまけ​

以下の

"He fought bizarre underground beings in the caves of Burma, was wounded by a laser before it was invented, and had a background with the OSS."

という話は初耳。

Maury Island UFO: The Crisman Conspiracy Paperback – October 1, 1999 by Kenn Thomas (Author)

In 1947 six flying saucers circled above a harbor boat in Puget Sound near Tacoma, Washington, one wobbling and spewing slag. The falling junk killed a dog and burned a boy's arm. His father, Harold Dahl, witnessed it all. The Maury Island incident became the first UFO event of the modern era. Then came Fred Crisman. Crisman was one of the most curious characters in the UFO lore and the history of covert intelligence. He fought bizarre underground beings in the caves of Burma, was wounded by a laser before it was invented, and had a background with the OSS. Harold Dahl told him about the Maury Island UFO. The next day Crisman witnessed another, single saucer... or did he?

ref: Amazon.com: Maury Island UFO: The Crisman Conspiracy: 9781881532194: Thomas, Kenn: Books https://www.amazon.com/Maury-Island-UFO-Crisman-Conspiracy

(2025-06-29)

entry.title: 1947年の UFO 目撃多発 : その詳細データ
entry.content:
前置き​

大半の UFO ファン/マニアは 1947年の 6-7月に、これほど多発していたということを把握していない筈。

異常に多発していた状況。

その詳細データが以下。別記事の一部だが、別記事の情報源が長大なので埋もれている。そこで該当箇所をピンポイントで示しておく。

詳細データ​

時系列

コメント​

以下、推測。

1947年の 6-7月にかけて、宇宙線や太陽フレアなどの一時的かつ強烈な増大が起きていたのではないか。それにより、orb や大気中での発光現象が発生しやすくなった。その orb や大気中の発光現象を UFO だと誤解した。

当時は人工衛星もなく、観測機器も未発達だったので観測データは期待できそうにない。

(2025-06-29)

entry.title: AI 分析 : Ted Bloeche : 1947年の UFO 目撃多発に関する調査報告書
entry.content:
前置き​

190ページに及ぶ長大な pdf 文書

Ted Bloecher, "Report On The UFO Wave of 1947", 1967

を AI で整理した。

この pdf 文書は過去記事、

❑ Ted Bloeche : 1947年の UFO 目撃多発に関する調査報告書 （途中1） (2023-06-19)

で取り上げて、放置したままだった。

情報源 :​

http://kirkmcd.princeton.edu/JEMcDonald/bloecher_67.pdf

AI

音声対話

https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/ab8088fe-0aef-45fd-a37a-08a094318d5a/audio

AI

UFO目撃報告：1947年夏の時系列記録

提供された文書は、主に1947年夏に北米で発生した未確認飛行物体（UFO）の目撃情報に関する包括的な分析です。これは、ジェームズ・F・マクドナルドによる序文と、テッド・ブローカーによる報告書で構成されています。

ブローカーは、当時の新聞記事を詳細に検証し、目撃情報の発生状況、目撃者の種類、物体の形状や動きに関する記述をまとめることに焦点を当てています。また、報告書は、軍や科学界による初期の反応と、いくつかの目撃情報が後にデマと判明した事例についても触れています。

目的は、UFO現象の初期段階におけるジャーナリズムの役割と、その後の政府の対応を記録することにあり、特にケネス・アーノルドの目撃情報が報道の引き金となったことが強調されています。

AI

詳細ブリーフィング資料：1947年の未確認飛行物体（UFO）報告書主要テーマと重要事実

概要​

提供された資料は、1947年夏にアメリカ合衆国を席巻した大規模なUFO目撃の波、通称「フラップ」に関する包括的な調査報告書からの抜粋です。この報告書は、目撃された物体の形態、機動、目撃者の種類、および経験的証拠を詳細に分類し、当時の公式見解と矛盾する広範な目撃情報を浮き彫りにしています。特に、ケネス・アーノルドによる有名な目撃事例とそれに続くメディアの反応、そして政府および軍当局の混乱した対応が強調されています。

主要テーマと重要なアイデア・事実​

  1. 1947年の「フラップ」現象とその定義

1947年の夏に発生したUFO目撃の波は、当時の空軍プロジェクト・ブルーブックの元責任者エドワード・J・ルッペルトによって「フラップ」と定義されました。彼は「フラップ」を「集団の、高度な混乱状態であって、まだパニック寸前ではない状況」と説明しています。資料は、この期間に非常に多くの人々が経験した著しい混乱が、このUFOの波を間違いなく「フラップ」のカテゴリーに入れると指摘しています。

  1. 目撃された物体の多様な形態と機動

報告書は、目撃されたUFOの形態と機動について詳細な分類を提供しています。

形態:​

  • 円盤状/皿型: 最も多く報告された形態で、「丸い物体」や「円盤」と表現されることが多かった（I-5）。「銀色で高度に研磨された」円盤状の物体が軸上で回転している様子や（I-2）、通常のディナープレートくらいの大きさで緑色の物体（II-16）などが報告されています。

  • V字型・三角形・翼型: V字型編隊や翼型の物体も複数報告されています（II-3, II-17）。特に、J.V.ワッツ・ジュニアが目撃した「V字編隊で飛行し、上下に揺れ動く」翼型の物体は、「円盤」や「皿」とは異なると強調されています（II-17）。

  • 魚雷型/円筒型: 「マヨネーズの瓶のような形をした物体」（II-16, III-9）や「煙突の形に似ている」と表現された物体も記録されています。

  • ドーム、フィン、つまみなどの突起物: ドーム型やフィン（尾部）を持つ円盤も報告されています（II-13）。「下向きに突き出た小さな尾」を持つ物体（II-14）も言及されています。

  • 小さな物体と「親と子」の関係:「ママディスク」の周りを「小さな赤ちゃんディスク」が飛び回り、その後「ママディスクが赤ちゃんディスクを吸収する」という非常に珍しい報告もあります（II-18）。

機動:​

  • 高速移動: ケネス・アーノルドの目撃事例では、物体が50マイルの距離を1分42秒で移動し、時速1,700マイルという驚異的な速度で飛行していたと計算されました（I-3）。他の報告でも「非常に速い」（I-15, I-16）、「途方もない速度」（I-7）といった表現が見られます。

  • 急激な上昇・下降、停止と反転:「急激な高度変化」（I-10）や「空中での突然の停止」（II-12）、「急降下して視界から消える」（III-2）といった、通常の航空機では考えられない機動が報告されています。

  • ホバリング: 空中での停止やホバリングも記録されています（I-6）。

  • 揺れ動く・ふらつくような飛行:「ふらつくような飛行パターン」（III-10）や「揺れながら、その後まっすぐになる」（付録-5）、「ひらひらと舞うように」着陸する様子（II-12）も記述されています。

無音飛行: 多くの目撃者が物体からの音を報告していません（I-2, II-12, II-15）。

  1. 目撃者の信頼性と多様性

目撃者のリストは、社会の幅広い層にわたる多様な専門家が含まれていることを示しています。これには以下が含まれます。

  • 航空専門家: 航空会社、軍、および民間パイロット（III-9）、航空計器技師（III-17）、空軍の元偵察写真家（IV-5）。ケネス・アーノルド自身も4000時間以上の飛行経験を持つベテランパイロットであり、「有能なセールスマン」や「副保安官」としての信頼性が強調されています（I-3）。

  • 警察・法執行官: 多数の警察官や保安官代理が目撃し、公式報告書を提出しています（III-14）。

  • 科学者: 気象学者（III-2）、海軍研究所のミサイル専門家（I-4）、天文学者（I-5）。

  • その他: 実業家、教育者、ニュース記者、医師、公共当局者、技術者、主婦、理容師、歯科医、郵便局長など（I-5）。

これらの目撃者たちは、「信頼できる人物がでたらめを言うような人間ではない」と評されています（I-15）。

  1. 公式の対応と矛盾する説明 軍や政府当局からの公式声明は、しばしば矛盾しており、事態を混乱させました。

  • 初期の混乱と否定: 空軍当局は当初、「現象、あるいは誰かの想像の産物」とし、「さらなる調査を正当化するほどの事実が出ていない」と述べていました（I-6）。また、一部の専門家は「計器盤の反射」「奇妙な雲の形成」「錯覚」といった説明を提供しています（I-7）。

  • ロズウェル事件の初期発表と訂正: ロズウェル陸軍航空隊の第509爆撃機群の諜報部隊が「円盤の破片を入手した」と発表したことは「原子爆弾の爆発に匹敵する影響」を与えましたが、直後に「高高度気象観測装置の残骸」と訂正されました（I-9）。

  • 「レーダーチャフ」説: ポートランドでの多数の円盤型物体の目撃は、空軍の公式ファイルでは「レーダーチャフ」（敵レーダーを混乱させるために投下されるアルミニウム片）と説明されていますが、これは繰り返される目撃には合致しないと指摘されています（viii）。

  • 軍高官の関心: 当時の陸軍航空隊司令官カール・スパーツ将軍が、ライトフィールドの当局に「円盤が何であるかを調査し、確認する」よう要請したこと（I-6）は、初期の公的な否定とは対照的に、内部での関心があったことを示唆しています。

これらの対応は、空軍の主要な関心事が「科学的調査ではなく、むしろ広報であったことを明確に示している」と結論付けられています（I-6）。

  1. 経験的証拠の存在と未解明な点 目撃報告に加えて、物体との相互作用や痕跡に関する報告も含まれています。

  • 電磁気効果: UFOが車両のヘッドライトや無線に影響を与えた例が報告されています（IV-3）。

  • 破片・痕跡:ボブ・スコットの庭で発見された、触っても熱くない「トーチのように明るい」物体（IV-2）。

  • モーリー島事件では、ダールが目撃したドーナツ型物体が「大量の金属片を噴出し」、彼のボートを損傷させ、息子を負傷させたという報告がありました（I-14）。ただし、これらは後に虚偽であったことが示唆されています（I-15）。

  • 動物の反応: 動物がUFOに反応したという報告も含まれています（IV-1）。

  • 写真: 報告書には複数のUFOの写真や絵が掲載されており、特にフランク・ライマンによるレイクシティでの写真（IV-3）や、ヒックスによるルイビルでの写真（IV-4）などが紹介されています。

  1. ケネス・アーノルドの目撃の重要性

ケネス・アーノルドの1947年6月24日のマウント・レーニア上空での目撃は、「現代のUFO活動の導入」として位置づけられています（I-2）。彼の目撃は、「空飛ぶ円盤（flying saucers）」という言葉を生み出し、その後の目撃の波の引き金となりました。彼の詳細な報告と、時速1,200マイルという推定速度は、当時の航空技術では説明がつかないものでした。

結論​

1947年のUFO「フラップ」は、単なる大衆ヒステリーでは片付けられない、広範で多様な目撃と証拠を含む複雑な現象でした。多岐にわたる信頼できる目撃者の存在、物体の異常な形態と機動、そしてそれに対する政府機関の混乱した、時に矛盾する対応は、この出来事が当時の社会に与えた大きな影響を示しています。この報告書は、後のUFO研究における重要な基礎資料として位置づけられるものです。

AI

タイムライン

1946年9月​

  • 日時不明、デラウェア州ルイス近郊: パイロットのフォレスト・ウェニヨンが「マヨネーズ瓶のような形をした物体」を初めて目撃する。

1947年5月​

  • 5月最終週、サウスカロライナ州セントヘレナ湾近郊: オーガスタ、ジョージア州の医師コールデン・R・バッティ博士が、南東方向に猛スピードで飛行する4つの円盤状の物体の編隊を目撃する。それらは軸上で回転しているように見え、高度約20,000フィートで、銀色に輝き「高度に研磨されている」ようだった。

1947年6月​

  • 6月2日、デラウェア州ルイス近郊: パイロットのフォレスト・ウェニヨンが、以前にも目撃した「マヨネーズ瓶のような形をした物体」が飛行機の前を横切るのを目撃する。これは空軍ファイルに「ミサイル」として記載されている。
  • 6月2日、オロビル、カリフォルニア州のフェザー川近郊: ロバート・ラーキンが3つの暗い物体を目撃する。そのうち1つはとがっていて傘のようだった。
  • 6月21日、ワシントン州モーリー島: ハーバーパトロールマンのハロルド・ダールがドーナツ状の物体6つを目撃。うち1つが大量の金属片を噴出し、ボートを損傷させ、息子を負傷させる。
  • 6月23日、カリフォルニア州ベーカーズフィールド: ベテラン飛行士のリチャード・ランキンが、正午ごろにV字型編隊で飛行する10個の平らな円形の物体を目撃する。
  • 6月23日、オレゴン州ラ・グランド: ラ・グランド高校生のリーランド・ジョーンズと2人のカトリック修道女が、V字型編隊で「編隊から出たり入ったり」する9つの円盤状の物体を目撃する。それらは「明るく丸く、ひれがついているようだった」とジョーンズは述べる。
  • 6月24日、ワシントン州レーニア山近郊: 事業でチヘリスからヤキマへ飛行中のケネス・アーノルドが、9つの明るくきらめく、平らな円盤状の物体が「飛び跳ねるように」動くのを目撃する。彼は後にその速度を時速1,700マイルと推定する。この目撃は「空飛ぶ円盤」という用語の導入に繋がる。
  • 6月24日、オレゴン州ウキア近郊: 鉱山技師のフレッド・ジョンソンがひれまたは尾を持つ5、6個の円盤を目撃する。
  • 6月27日、シアトル、ワシントン州: 空軍ファイルに記載されているケース46とケース84が関連するが、詳細は不明。
  • 6月28日～30日: 合衆国30州とカナダ2州で合計128件の目撃情報が報告され、そのうち90件が昼間の目撃だった。ワシントン州が最多で20件、オレゴン州とニューメキシコ州がそれぞれ13件だった。
  • 6月29日、ニューメキシコ州ホワイトサンズ: 海軍研究室のミサイル専門家カール・J・ゾーンが目撃する（詳細は不明だが、空軍ファイルには未確認とは分類されていない）。
  • 6月30日、グランドキャニオン近郊: 海軍パイロットが2つの物体が地球に落下するのを目撃する（空軍ファイルには未確認とは分類されていない）。
  • 6月30日、ワシントン州スポケーン: 郡夜間刑務官のジョン・モーニングが、街の上空を西から飛んでくる「丸い物体」を目撃し、公式報告書を提出する。
  • 6月30日、アイダホ州ヘイリー近郊: ウォルター・ニッチが空飛ぶ円盤を目撃する。
  • 6月30日、テキサス州デカルブ近郊: 農民のウェンデル・L・カーソンが、彼と幼い息子がトマト畑を高度100フィートで音もなく横切る円盤を目撃する。「鏡のように太陽を反射していた」と彼は説明する。
  • 6月30日、ポートランド、オレゴン州: ポートランド気象局長E・S・エリソン大佐が、気象観測用気球について言及し、それらが円盤のような速度に達することはできないと述べる。

1947年7月​

  • 7月1日～2日: マップ#8に示された地域で目撃情報が報告される。
  • 7月3日: マップ#9に示された地域で目撃情報が報告される。
  • 7月3日、アイダホ州セントマリーズ近郊: ウォルター・ジョンソン夫人が、南の空から飛んでくる「洗濯桶」のような9つの大きな物体（一部は8つと数える）のゆるい編隊を目撃する。それらは「素早く現れ、ぎくしゃく止まり、葉のように地上にひらひらと舞い降りた」という。
  • 7月4日、ワシントン州レイクシティ: 沿岸警備隊のフランク・ライマンが、レイクシティ上空を飛ぶ円盤を撮影する（広く公開された最初の写真）。
  • 7月4日、オレゴン州ポートランド: 警察官のフレッド・クライブス、クラレンス・マッケイ、ジョン・サリバンが、ダークで「派手ではない」が「ガチョウの群れ」のように見える物体がV字型で飛んでいるのを目撃する。彼らは「低いハミング音」または「ドローン音」を聞いたと報告する。
  • 7月4日、アイダホ州ツインフォールズ: ピクニックをしていた60人が、35以上の物体の3つの編隊が頭上を飛行するのを目撃する。
  • 7月4日、ワシントン州ハウザー湖近郊: スポケーン近郊のハウザー湖で200人以上が空の単一の円盤を目撃する。
  • 7月4日、アイダホ-オレゴン州境近郊: ユナイテッド航空機の全乗組員が、薄暮時に2つの円盤群を目撃する。
  • 7月4日、アイダホ州ボイシ: UPIのニュースマンと友人たちが、単一の円盤が猛スピードで頭上を直接飛行し、数秒で地平線に消えるのを目撃する。
  • 7月4日、アイダホ州エメット & オレゴン州オンタリオ: キャプテン・カーティス・J・スミスとスティーブンスが、当初は飛行機と間違えたが、平らで円形の物体を目撃する。彼らは客室乗務員のマーティ・モローを呼ぶ。
  • 7月4日、モンタナ州クレイグ近郊: グレートフォールズの芸術家で彫刻家のカート・デニスと妻が、ミズーリ川で釣りをしているときに、12個ほどの銀色の物体が「皿が連なって飛んでいる」ように見えるのを目撃する。
  • 7月4日、ノースダコタ州エリオット: 農民のヴァージル・ビーンが、母親の農場上空で「ディナープレートくらいの大きさで形は同じだが、緑色」の小さな物体を目撃する。彼の母親と兄弟も目撃する。
  • 7月4日、テキサス州ヒルズボロ: ボブ・スコットという農民の庭で、「たいまつ（溶接用トーチ）のように明るいが、拾ってもやけどしない」円盤状の物体が発見される。
  • 7月4日、ニューヨーク州マンハッタン: ニューヨーク市警察官のフランク・M・リッチモンドが、空を高速で移動する銀色の円盤状の物体を目撃する。
  • 7月5日: マップ#11に示された地域で目撃情報が報告される。
  • 7月5日、メリーランド州ベセスダ: ケース306の詳細が報告される。
  • 7月5日、カリフォルニア州ベイエリア: マップBに示された地域で目撃情報が報告される。
  • 7月5日、メイン州オーガスタ: ニュースマンでプログラムディレクターのダン・ケリーと友人が、オーガスタ市上空を北へ猛スピードで飛行する12個の円盤状の物体を目撃する。
  • 7月5日、アーカンソー州フェイエットビル: ホイットニー・L・ヴァンダーホーフ・ジュニアが空飛ぶ円盤を目撃する。
  • 7月5日、ニューハンプシャー州アルトン: チャールズ・M・デール知事の息子トーマス・デール（26歳、8年以上の飛行経験を持つベテラン）が、友人のジェレ・ステットソンと共に飛行中に「過剰な速度」で接近する奇妙な物体を目撃する。

全般的な情報​

  • 「フラップ」の定義: プロジェクト・ブルーブックの元責任者、エドワード・J・ルッペルトが「レポート・オン・未確認飛行物体」（1956年）で「フラップ」を「混乱状態にある集団の状態」と定義している。

  • 1947年夏のフラップ: 1947年夏に多くの人々が経験した混乱状態は、この期間のUFO現象を「フラップ」のカテゴリーに入れる。

  • 軍の反応: 当初、米空軍は目撃情報を「レーダー攪乱金属片」や「気象観測用気球」などの従来の説明で説明しようとする。矛盾する公式声明は、軍の主な関心が科学的調査ではなく広報であったことを示唆している。

  • 目撃者: 経営者、教育者、気象学者、軍人（陸軍、海軍、海兵隊、沿岸警備隊）、ニュース記者、医師、パイロット、警察官、公務員、エンジニア、科学者など、幅広い職業の人々が目撃者となる。

主要な著者・編集者・専門家

Ted Bloecher（テッド・ブローカー）:​

  • 本報告書「REPORT ON THE UFO WAVE OF 1947」の著者。彼の研究は、1947年夏にUFO問題が公衆に現れた際の「決定的な分析」と見なされている。彼は全国の図書館にある古い新聞ファイル、空軍のプロジェクト・ブルーブックのファイル、および独立した調査グループのファイルを参照して、1947年の膨大なUFO報告を系統的に整理しました。

Dr. James E. McDonald（ジェームズ・E・マクドナルド博士）:​

本報告書の序文を執筆したアリゾナ大学大気物理学研究所の主任物理学者。彼は、UFO問題が「おそらく人類が直面する最も傑出した科学的問題である」と信じていると述べています。彼は、1947年の中頃の目撃報告が、単なる数十件ではなく数百件に上ったことに「呆然とした」と述べており、このエピソードが記録上「際立った目撃波」の一つであると強調しています。

Dr. J. Allen Hynek（J・アレン・ハイネック博士）:​

  • 空軍のUFO調査における科学顧問。1947年当時、プロジェクト・サインのためにケネス・アーノルドの報告をレビューした際、「矛盾点」を発見したとされています。具体的には、物体の速度と距離の推定と、物体のサイズの推定を一致させることが問題でした。彼は、空軍のファイルにおける平均的なUFO目撃報告率が1日1〜2件であると述べています。

Edward J. Ruppelt（エドワード・J・ラペルト）:​

  • 元プロジェクト・ブルーブックの責任者。彼の著書「The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects」の中で、「フラップ」という状態を「混乱の進んだ状態にある人々のグループの状況」と定義しています。彼はまた、1947年のミューロック空軍基地での目撃が「空軍にUFOへの深い関心を持たせた最初の目撃」であったと述べています。

Charles Fort（チャールズ・フォート）:​
